treaty_name: Agreement between the Kingdom of Norway and the Republic of Singapore for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income (1997, as amended 2009)
eif_quote: Lovdata metadata: "Avtalens ikrafttredelsesdato 17-04-1998" | Art. 29(2): "The Agreement shall enter into force on the date of receipt of the later of these notifications and shall thereupon have effect in respect of taxes on income relating to the calendar year (including accounting periods beginning in any such year) next following that in which the Agreement enters into force and subsequent years."
source_title: Lovdata Norges traktater (English version), Agreement Norway-Singapore 1997 and amending Protocol of 18 September 2009 (both authentic in English only)

rates.quote: a. 5 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends if the beneficial owner is a company which holds directly at least 25 per cent of the capital of the company paying the dividends;
b. 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends in all other cases.

However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the interest, the tax so charged shall not exceed 7 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the royalties, the tax so charged shall not exceed 7 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.basis: none (MLI not applicable: Singapore lists Norway but Norway does not list Singapore; no PPT/main-purpose clause in the Agreement)

notes: Not MLI-covered, so no PPT and no MLI Art. 8 holding period. Art. 10(8)(a): Singapore levies no tax on dividends beyond the tax on company profits (imputation/one-tier), so in practice the Art. 10(2) limits bite only on Norwegian-source dividends; Art. 10(8)(b): if Singapore introduces a dividend tax, the Art. 10(2) limits apply. Art. 10(3)-(4) and 10(8)(b): dividends paid to the Government of Singapore (MAS, GIC, agreed bodies) exempt from Norwegian tax, and vice versa for the Government of Norway (Central Bank, Petroleum Fund, National Insurance Fund) - not modelled. Art. 11(3)-(4): interest paid to the other Government (incl. MAS, GIC, ECICS; Norwegian local authorities, Central Bank, GIEK, Eksportfinans etc.) exempt at source (not modelled). The 2009 Protocol (in force 2010-04-04) replaced only Art. 27 (exchange of information). Replaced the 1984 Convention from 1999.
